starving.title: Starving Dinosaur
starving.message: {species} in enclosure {enclosure} has had nothing to eat for days and is losing health. Buy {food} from the General Store, or open the enclosure in the Park view and feed it directly.
starving.tooltip: Food is a daily cost that never stops. Every dinosaur eats a set number of units per day; keep park stock ahead of that number.

events.title: Breakout!
events.message: A dinosaur pushed through a weak spot in its fence and wandered onto the visitor path. The park closed early while staff rounded it up. Fence condition dropped and visitors are nervous.
events.tooltip: A cheap fence saves money today but a breakout costs far more later. Match the fence to the dinosaur.

events.title: Fence Too Weak
events.message: One of your dinosaurs is bigger than its fence can handle. It leaned on a segment until it snapped. Nobody was hurt, but the pen needs repairs and the crowd went home early.
events.tooltip: Every species has a minimum fence tier. Going under it is a gamble that gets worse every day.

events.title: Midnight Wanderer
events.message: Security cameras caught a dinosaur strolling through the parking lot at 2 a.m. It was back in its pen by morning, but the local paper ran the story on the front page.
events.tooltip: Security staff cost a salary every month, but they catch problems before they become news.

events.title: Sick Dinosaur
events.message: One of your dinosaurs stopped eating and is looking sluggish. Without a vet on staff it will keep losing health each day until it recovers on its own, if it does.
events.tooltip: A vet is insurance. You pay a little every month so one bad week does not cost you a whole dinosaur.

events.title: Bug Going Around
events.message: Something is spreading between pens. Several dinosaurs are off their food and running low on energy. Vets can slow it down and keep it from spreading further.
events.tooltip: More animals means more risk. As the park grows, the staff that protects it has to grow too.

events.title: Spoiled Feed
events.message: A batch of food went bad in the heat and a dinosaur got sick eating it. The spoiled stock had to be thrown out.
events.tooltip: Stock costs money to buy and money to keep. Buying way more than you need is not always the safe choice.

events.title: Staff Walkout
events.message: An employee handed in their notice and left the same day. Nobody is covering their job until you hire a replacement at the Employment Office.
events.tooltip: People are part of your costs, but they are also part of your park. A manager keeps the team from falling apart.

events.title: Burned Out
events.message: Your crew is stretched too thin. Two staff members quit at once, saying there was too much work and nobody in charge.
events.tooltip: Past a certain size, a park needs a manager. Skipping that salary can cost you two other people.

events.title: Hired Away
events.message: A rival attraction across town offered one of your best people a raise. They took it. Your remaining staff are wondering if they should ask for more too.
events.tooltip: Other businesses want good workers too. Keeping people happy is cheaper than replacing them.

events.title: Thunderstorm
events.message: A heavy storm rolled through overnight. Fences took a beating, a few paths flooded, and the park had to stay closed while the crew cleaned up.
events.tooltip: Weather is a cost you cannot plan around exactly, so keep some cash in reserve for surprises.

events.title: Heat Wave
events.message: A week of brutal heat kept visitors at home and left the dinosaurs tired and thirsty. Attendance is down until the weather breaks.
events.tooltip: Even the best season has bad weeks. Do not spend all of a good month's money before the month is over.

events.title: Snowed In
events.message: A snowstorm shut the roads. Nobody could reach the park for days, and a section of fence collapsed under the weight of the snow.
events.tooltip: Winter is slow anyway. A storm on top of that is why winter cash planning matters most.

events.title: TV Crew Visits
events.message: A local news station filmed a story about your park. It aired tonight and people loved it. Expect a crowd this week.
events.tooltip: Free attention works like a free ad campaign. A clean, interesting park earns it more often.

events.title: Video Goes Viral
events.message: A visitor's clip of your dinosaurs at feeding time spread everywhere online. Ticket demand is way up for a while.
events.tooltip: A sudden crowd is only good if you can handle it. Gate and parking capacity set the ceiling on your best days.

events.title: Glowing Review
events.message: A travel writer gave your park top marks for being clean and well run. Families are planning trips because of it.
events.tooltip: Reputation builds slowly and pays off for a long time. Keeping the park clean is an investment, not a chore.

events.title: Generous Gift
events.message: A dinosaur lover who visited last month sent a check to support your work. No strings attached.
events.tooltip: Extra cash is a chance, not a plan. Use a windfall to pay down debt or build something that keeps earning.

events.title: Research Grant
events.message: A science foundation awarded your park a grant for taking good care of rare species. The money arrives this week.
events.tooltip: Doing things well can open doors you did not plan for. The vet you hired for safety just paid for itself.

events.title: Fossil Found
events.message: While digging a new fence post, your crew uncovered a real fossil. A museum bought it for their collection.
events.tooltip: Some income is luck. Count on the steady stuff, like tickets, and treat luck as a bonus.

events.title: Holiday Weekend
events.message: A long weekend brought families from all over. The gates were packed and the food stand sold out twice.
events.tooltip: Big days are where concessions shine. Every extra visitor spends a little more than the ticket price.

events.title: School Field Trips
events.message: Three local schools booked field trips this week. Buses of kids are arriving every morning.
events.tooltip: Attendance changes with the calendar. Spring and fall bring school groups; plan staff and food for it.

events.title: Summer Rush
events.message: School is out and the weather is perfect. Visitors are lining up before the gates even open.
events.tooltip: Summer is the busy season. Money made now has to cover the quiet winter months.

_notes: M2.6: staff_quit-type weights halved. Escape-type random events need requires_breakout_risk: an enclosure whose daily breakout chance (fences.json breakout rules) is above zero; a well-fenced small herbivore never triggers them. Every positive event now needs at least one living dinosaur (requires_dinos): a park whose animals have all starved cannot be carried by donations, media boosts or holiday crowds.
